note: SHARED between mobile and webapp. Both repos run these exact cases against their own timezone module. Keep the two copies byte-identical; timezoneParity.test asserts it when the sibling repo is present. Add a case here whenever a timezone bug is fixed in EITHER repo, so the other inherits the regression test instead of shipping the same defect.

cases.why: A stored scheduled_time of '24:00' rendered as '12:00 PM' in BOTH repos on 2026-08-31 — twelve hours wrong on a medication time. Guards existed at three other readers in each file but not in the shared renderer.
Same defect in the 24-hour cycle: raw, this printed '24:15'.
The guard must not fold real noon.

Parsed without the Z in BOTH repos, giving noon in the DEVICE zone — an instant skewed by up to 14h, which decides DST comparisons. Webapp's sweep caught it in 6 of 10 zones; mobile's stayed green because its test used a local getter.
At noon UTC on the US transition day Denver has moved to MDT and Phoenix has not, so the zones genuinely differ and a dual line is required. With the device-local parse this flipped by device.
An older hour-of-day fold reported +14 as -10, which made timezonesAreDifferent(Kiritimati, Honolulu) false and hid the dual line for the pairs that break.
